sections.title: Dynamics (Chapter 4)
formulas: a = g[sin(θ) - μ_k·cos(θ)] (Motion on an inclined plane with friction)
principles: Newton's First Law: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion unless acted upon by an external force
Newton's Second Law: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass
Newton's Third Law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction

sections.title: Circular Motion and Gravitation (Chapter 5)
principles: Objects moving in circular paths require a centripetal force pointing toward the center
Universal gravitation acts between all objects with mass
Kepler's First Law: Planets orbit in ellipses with the sun at one focus
Kepler's Second Law: Planets sweep out equal areas in equal times
Kepler's Third Law: Square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis

sections.title: Work and Energy (Chapter 6)
principles: Work is the transfer of energy through force applied over a distance
Conservation of energy: Total energy remains constant in an isolated system
Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred

sections.title: Harmonics (Chapter 11)
formulas: E = ½kA² (Energy in simple harmonic oscillator)
k = m(2πf)² (Spring constant from mass and frequency)
principles: Simple harmonic motion results when a restoring force is proportional to displacement
Pendulums and spring-mass systems are examples of harmonic oscillators
Constructive interference: waves add together
Destructive interference: waves cancel out
Maximum velocity in SHM occurs at equilibrium position

sections.title: Electromagnetism (Chapters 16 and 17)
formulas: F = qE (Force on charge in electric field)
V = kq/r (Electric potential of point charge)
C = κε₀A/d (Capacitance of parallel plate capacitor)
principles: Like charges repel, opposite charges attract
Electric fields point from positive to negative charge
Electric potential decreases with distance from a point charge
Methods of charging: friction, contact, induction

sections.title: Electricity (Chapters 18 and 19)
principles: Current flows from high to low potential
Current is conserved at junctions (Kirchhoff's current law)
Sum of voltage changes around a loop is zero (Kirchhoff's voltage law)
Resistors in series have the same current
Resistors in parallel have the same voltage
